title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) of the Lumbar Spine
summary: Covers non-emergent MRI of the lumbar spine after documented failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative management, or immediately in presence of red flag signs (cauda equina syndrome, progressive neurological deficit, active cancer history, infection).

sections.title: Indications and Limitations of Coverage
sections.content:
Lumbar spine MRI (CPT 72148) is considered medically necessary when ANY of the following criteria are met:
1. Red Flag Signs: Immediate MRI indicated for progressive neurological deficit (e.g. progressive motor weakness), suspicion of cauda equina syndrome (bowel/bladder dysfunction, saddle anesthesia), known active malignancy with new back pain, or clinical suspicion of spinal infection/osteomyelitis (fever, elevated ESR/CRP, IV drug use history).
2. Radiculopathy with Failure of Conservative Therapy: Severe radiating radicular pain persisting after a minimum of 6 weeks of active documented conservative management (including physical therapy, structured home exercise, NSAIDs or neuropathic pain medication).
3. Post-surgical evaluation: Persistent or recurrent symptoms following lumbar spine surgery within 12 months.

sections.title: Exclusions and Non-Covered Scenarios
sections.content: MRI is not covered for uncomplicated acute low back pain (< 6 weeks duration) without radicular symptoms or neurological signs. Repeat MRI within 6 months without new neurological deficits or acute trauma is considered not medically necessary.

criteria.title: Red Flag Signs or Neurological Emergency
criteria.description: Documented acute red flag symptoms: cauda equina syndrome (bowel/bladder incontinence, saddle anesthesia), progressive motor weakness, or active malignancy.
criteria.required_evidence: Physical exam or clinical documentation showing progressive motor deficit, bowel/bladder dysfunction, or oncologic history with localized bone pain.

criteria.title: Documented Radicular Symptoms
criteria.description: Presence of true radicular symptoms radiating below the knee in a dermatomal distribution with positive straight leg raise or nerve root irritation signs.
criteria.required_evidence: Documented radiating nerve root pain or positive neural tension sign (positive straight leg raise, dermatomal sensory loss, or reflex asymmetry).

criteria.title: Failure of Conservative Therapy (>= 6 weeks)
criteria.description: Trial of at least 6 consecutive weeks of conservative management consisting of formal physical therapy, prescribed medication (NSAIDs or oral steroids or neuropathic agents), and activity modification within the past 6 months.
criteria.required_evidence: Clinical notes or therapy discharge summary specifying at least 6 weeks of PT/medication trial with dates and lack of functional improvement.

criteria.title: No Uncomplicated Non-Specific Back Pain Exclusion
criteria.description: Exclusion applies if pain is non-specific axial lower back pain of less than 6 weeks duration without neurologic involvement.
criteria.required_evidence: Rule out non-specific axial back pain lacking duration or neurological findings.
